newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up on local demand, little support.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up on local demand, little support.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Wednesday on local speculation following the rise in the Dow Jones index and Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on Tuesday, traders said.
But they said it was difficult to forecast where the market would go during the day, as they were waiting to see whether investors in London and New York would follow through.
Prices have been coming off recently after the market advanced 30 percent in June, and it is unclear whether foreign investors will re-ignite the Russian rally.
At 0810 GMT metals plant Norilsk Nickel rose to $13.75 from $13.40 at Tuesday's close, LUKoil was $22.00 after $21.15, Mosenergo edged up to $1.530 from $1.496.
"There was a rise in the morning, even some feverish demand," said Alfa-Capital Chief Trader Mikhail Khaleyev.
"Now people have stopped trying to understand what will happen later. The growth happened purely on the Russian wish of a rise, I cannot see any real support."

Traders said the market rose after a gain of nearly 155 percent in the Dow Jones index on Tuesday and Greenspan's comments, which were taken by former Fed officials and Wall Street experts to indicate that there would be no rise in U.S. interest rates in the near future.

Aton broker Boris Shvedsky said Russian operators were trying to invest new funds, which were coming in from the government securities market and from new clients eager to open positions in leading shares.

He also said news First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov would on Wednesday present President Boris Yeltsin with a draft decree allowing the issue of convertible bonds by national power utility UES pushed up the price of the share, which dragged all other shares up with it.

Russian agencies said the decree on the bonds, which are expected to hit international markets this autumn, would raise five trillion roubles ($870 million) intended to pay wage arrears. It needs Yeltsin's signature to come into force.
